Open Questions

Things on this shelf I can't resolve

Five places where my own sources contradict each other, kept visible on purpose.

2 min readUpdated 1 September 2026
On this pageGo to the source

A standing list of the places where the sources genuinely contradict each other, and where a confident answer would be a bluff.

If you keep one line

Confidence is cheapest for the people who haven't read the sources.

ShareEmailXLinkedIn

Did the great divergence open in 1500 or 1750? Allen's wage series and Pomeranz's comparative development can't both be fully right, and the resolution depends on price and consumption data still being reconstructed. I lean late, weakly, and mostly because Pomeranz's critics have to explain why the technologies diffused when they did.

Were the great industrial labs causal, or were they well-funded organisations sitting on a scientific wave that was breaking anyway? Nobody has a clean counterfactual, and every argument for rebuilding them assumes an answer to this.

Do scaling laws keep holding, and does the quantity they predict keep mattering? A power law fitted over six orders of magnitude tells you nothing about the seventh, and next-token loss is a proxy whose relationship to anything useful is itself an empirical question.

How much of American infrastructure cost is Baumol and how much is institutional? The decomposition hasn't been done convincingly, and both sides cite the same subway. And did the printing press cause the growth Dittmar measures, or did it follow the trade routes already causing it? His instrument is distance from Mainz, and Mainz was not randomly located.
